_about: How much an ingredient's own reference data (ICSC, CAMEO, NIOSH) counts, by its concentration in the product. Edit the numbers here; tools/refgate.py reads this file. Approved 27 Nov 2026 as a starting point.
concentration_basis: top of the Section 3 range (e.g. 5-<16 % counts as 16 %); a single value counts as itself; '>= x' alone counts as x

bands._about: major: top of range > major_above_percent (so "≤ 10 %" is minor); minor: >= minor_min_percent up to major_above_percent; trace: below minor_min_percent. Changed 27 Nov 2026 from ">= 10" after the user review of the blind test.

major._about: > major_above_percent: reference data can drive fails and warnings as before.

minor._about: minor_min_percent up to major_above_percent: warning or info only, and only where the data fits the mixture's own classification (kind_fits). Explosive/peroxide/water-reactive and toxic-gas-release data always fit (capped at max_severity). General reactivity data (incompatible families) fits every mixture but is capped at general_reactivity_max.

trace._about: < minor_min_percent: ignored, except explosive, peroxide-forming or water-reactive data (kind high_hazard), capped at max_severity.

kind_fits._about: kind of reference statement -> hazard codes in the MIXTURE's own classification that make it relevant. A minor ingredient's statement of that kind is dropped unless the mixture carries at least one of these codes.

physical_form._about: Data for a gas (or liquefied/refrigerated gas) apply only if the product is a gas or an aerosol; dust/powder statements apply only if the product is a solid.

unclassified_mixture._about: A mixture SDS with no hazard classification in Section 2: findings based only on reference data are capped at max_severity (user decision, 27 Nov 2026).
